title: Coulomb's Law
learning_goal: Use Coulomb's law to predict the magnitude and direction of electric force between charged objects.

stages.title: 1. Electric charges exert forces
stages.content: Like charges repel and opposite charges attract. The electric force acts along the line connecting the two charges.

stages.title: 2. Coulomb's law
stages.content: The magnitude of electric force is F = k|q₁q₂|/r², where k is Coulomb's constant, q₁ and q₂ are the charges, and r is the distance between them.

stages.title: 3. Worked example
stages.content: If the distance between two charges doubles while the charges stay the same, the electric force becomes one-fourth as large because 1/(2²) = 1/4.

stages.title: 4. Determine attraction or repulsion
stages.content: Use the signs of the charges to determine direction. Same signs repel. Opposite signs attract. Use the equation for magnitude and the charge signs for direction.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: Two charged particles remain unchanged, but their separation becomes half as large. By what factor does the electric force change?
stages.hint: Distance is squared in the denominator. Replace r with r/2.
stages.alternate_explanation: Halving the distance makes the denominator four times smaller, so the force becomes four times larger.
stages.answer: The electric force becomes 4 times as large.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, use F = k|q₁q₂|/r², predict force changes from charge and distance, and determine whether two charges attract or repel.

concept_cards.title: How does doubling the separation of fixed point charges change force magnitude?
concept_cards.content: Coulomb’s law is F = k|q₁q₂|/r². Doubling r multiplies r² by four.

concept_cards.title: Two charges have opposite signs. What is the direction of their electric interaction?
concept_cards.content: The force on each charge points toward the other. Equal-sign charges instead repel.
